full_judgment:
Abu Sayeed Ahammed, J: This Rule under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the defendant No. 2, arises out of the judgment and decree dated 31.7.88 and 7.8.88 respectively passed in other class Appeal No. 31 of 1987, by the District Judge, Gaibandha, affirming the judgment and decree dated 29.11.86 and 4.12.86 respectively, passed by the Subordinate Judge, Gaibandha, in other Class Suit No. 145 of 1985, decreeing the suit for declaration that the deed of transfer dated 10.10.84 selling the suit land comprising 6.85 acres, by Patani Sungari Dasya, a widow (defendant No. 1) having her life interest only in the suit land, which she had inherited after the death of her husband Bishwanath Das, to Shibnath Das, the present petitioner (the defendant No. 2), younger brother of said Bishwnath Das, is not binding upon the plaintiffs (Opposite Parties Nos. 1-6) who had brought the suit in the capacity as reversioners. 

 5. Both parties adduced oral and documentary evidence. Each party examined 5 witnesses including said Patani Sundari Dasya, Shibnath, Bimala and Sunil Chandra Sale deed in question is Ext. B and another document has been filed on behalf of the plaintiffs showing value of the land in the locality at the relevant time which has been marked as X. Courts below decreed the suit concurrently disbelieving the case of the defendants that the sale of the suit land was made for legal necessity. 

 (1) Where a widow or other limited heir alienates property inherited by her in contravention of the provisions of 178, the next reversioner, though he has no interest higher than a chance of succession, may institute a suit in her lifetime for a declaration that the alienation is not binding on the reversioner and if the facts are proved, the Court may pass a decree declaring that the alienation is not valid beyond the lifetime of the limited heir. 

 12. In view of the facts and circumstances and the discussions above, we hold that the Courts below rightly decreed the suit of the plaintiffs and committed no error of law. However, regard being had to the provision of Section 205 of the Hindu Law, we are of the view that the alienation of the suit land will remain valid during the lifetime of Patani Sundari Dasya to said Shibnath and it will not be binding upon the plaintiffs after her death. 

 13. The result is, therefore, the Rule is discharged with the modifications that the decrees passed by the Courts below shall be effective against the alliance of the suit land, and Shibnath after the death of Patani Sundari Dasya, the transferer of the same.
